question: Does an always-on JOEWRKS Common Core improve native Codex enough to justify its quality, coordination, and token cost?

caseResults.gainScope: subjective visual hierarchy, workflow adaptability, and one avoided empty search; not rough-request compilation itself

nonCompensatingFindings: All three regression cases preserved the required safe outcome but improved no quality item and were less efficient or less relevant than Control.
The explicit candidate rule to report stale handoff or recorded-PASS conflicts did not change either final report.
Both arms independently turned the rough request into a substantial local artifact, so that transformation was native behavior in this sample.

The rough candidate's visual, adaptability, and search-use wins do not cancel its separate scope, accessibility, maintainability, and cost regressions or the completion-report defect shared by both arms.
A 4.57% median meets the conditional 5% cost ceiling only as a necessary condition; material item-level regressions still prohibit promotion.
limitations: Each scenario is one paired stochastic run, so the result rejects promotion under this fixed contract rather than proving that every possible rule wording is universally harmful.
The rough artifact interaction comparison remained unverified after the generic checker selected a hidden custom input; static syntax, remote-reference, and Edge-render checks passed for both arms.
The experiment tests an always-on shared overlay. It does not reject concise project-specific AGENTS.md rules or task-triggered skills with unique value.

decision.reasonNoRevision: The candidate already states the missing conflict and scope rules, yet they showed no causal gain. Adding fixture-specific wording would be post-hoc overfitting.
decision.implementation: Point the install manifest to the one-byte no-common-core source so the deterministic installer retains an empty managed slot but adds no always-on instructions. Keep project-specific AGENTS.md and explicit or hybrid skills independent.
decision.reconsiderWhen: Only after a new repeated real-world failure is isolated and a shorter targeted intervention beats native Control without material regressions.
